tools.name: create_ceiling
tools.description: Create ceilings (forros) from a polygon in mm (with holes), a rectangle, or a room's boundary (inner finish face by default, optional boundaryOffset, e.g. -10 for a shadow gap). The ceiling type must be named; heightAboveLevel (mm) goes to 'Height Offset From Level'. Needs Revit 2022+. Every ceiling is read back (id, area m², height). One Ctrl+Z undoes the call.

boundary.description: Outline: points (+holes), rectangle, or a room (inner finish face by default).

points.description: Closed outline as plan points in mm (the last point connects back to the first; do not repeat the first point).

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

origin.description: Corner the rectangle starts from (before rotation), in mm.

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

width.description: Size along X (before rotation), in mm.

depth.description: Size along Y (before rotation), in mm.

rotation.description: Counter-clockwise rotation around the origin corner, in degrees. Default 0.

holes.description: Openings inside the outline (shafts, cut-outs). Only with points/rectangle.

points.description: Closed list of plan points in mm (do not repeat the first point).

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

room.description: Room whose boundary is used, by element id, room number or room name (ambiguous names fail with the candidates).

boundaryLocation.description: With room: which wall line bounds the outline. finish (default) = inner finish face of the walls; center = wall centreline; coreBoundary / coreCenter = wall core.

boundaryOffset.description: Grows (positive) or shrinks (negative) the whole outline, holes included, in mm. E.g. -10 leaves a 10 mm gap to the walls.

ceilingType.description: Ceiling type as "Family: Type", type name or id. Required: never chosen for you.

level.description: Level the height is measured from, by name or id. Optional with boundary.room (defaults to the room's level).

heightAboveLevel.description: Height of the ceiling above the level in mm (Revit's 'Height Offset From Level'), e.g. 2600.

continueOnError.description: false (default): any failure rolls back the whole call. true: failed items are skipped and listed in failed[].

tools.name: create_floor
tools.description: Create floors (slabs or finish floors) from a polygon in mm (with holes), a rectangle, or a room's boundary (inner finish face by default, optional boundaryOffset). The floor type must be named. heightOffset (mm) is written to 'Height Offset From Level', not baked into the outline. Every floor is read back (id, area m², thickness, offset). One Ctrl+Z undoes the call.

boundary.description: Outline: points (+holes), rectangle, or a room (inner finish face by default).

points.description: Closed outline as plan points in mm (the last point connects back to the first; do not repeat the first point).

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

origin.description: Corner the rectangle starts from (before rotation), in mm.

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

width.description: Size along X (before rotation), in mm.

depth.description: Size along Y (before rotation), in mm.

rotation.description: Counter-clockwise rotation around the origin corner, in degrees. Default 0.

holes.description: Openings inside the outline (shafts, cut-outs). Only with points/rectangle.

points.description: Closed list of plan points in mm (do not repeat the first point).

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

room.description: Room whose boundary is used, by element id, room number or room name (ambiguous names fail with the candidates).

boundaryLocation.description: With room: which wall line bounds the outline. finish (default) = inner finish face of the walls; center = wall centreline; coreBoundary / coreCenter = wall core.

boundaryOffset.description: Grows (positive) or shrinks (negative) the whole outline, holes included, in mm. E.g. -10 leaves a 10 mm gap to the walls.

floorType.description: Floor type as "Family: Type", type name or id. Required: never chosen for you.

level.description: Level by name or id. Optional with boundary.room (defaults to the room's level); required otherwise.

heightOffset.description: Height offset of the top of the floor from the level, in mm (Revit's 'Height Offset From Level'). Default 0.

structural.description: Mark the floor as structural. Default false.

continueOnError.description: false (default): any failure rolls back the whole call. true: failed items are skipped and listed in failed[].

tools.name: create_sheets
tools.description: Create sheets in batch (real or placeholder): number, name, title block ("Family: Type", default title block if omitted), extra parameters and optional views/schedules placed at x/y in mm. Numbers are checked for forbidden characters and collisions (also within the request) before anything is created; names are read back. One transaction (one Ctrl+Z); all or nothing unless continueOnError. Undo: Ctrl+Z, or delete the returned sheet ids.

items.description: Sheets to create, up to 200 per call.

number.description: Sheet number, unique in the document (e.g. "A-101").

titleBlock.description: Title block type as "Family: Type", type name or id. Omit for the document's default title block; "none" for no title block.

placeholder.description: Create a placeholder sheet (listed in sheet lists, not printed; no title block or views). Default false.

parameters.description: Extra sheet parameters by name, e.g. {"Desenhado por": "AE"}; same value rules as set_parameters.

views.description: Views or schedules to place on the new sheet.

view.description: View or schedule to place, by name or id.

x.description: Centre of the viewport on the sheet, from the sheet origin (bottom-left of most title blocks). Unit: mm.

y.description: Centre of the viewport on the sheet, from the sheet origin. Unit: mm.

continueOnError.description: false (default): any failure rolls back every sheet of the call. true: failed sheets are skipped and listed in failed[].

tools.name: create_walls
tools.description: Create walls by segment, polyline (open or closed) or rectangle, coordinates in mm. The wall type must be named (never defaulted); height is either a top level (+topOffset) or an unconnected height. locationLine says which face/centreline sits on the points (e.g. finishFaceInterior to draw the inner outline of a room); closed shapes put the exterior face outside. Returns ids, lengths and the read-back constraints. One Ctrl+Z undoes the call.

items.description: Walls to create: each item is a segment, a polyline or a rectangle.

shape.description: segment: one wall between 2 points. polyline: one wall per edge of the points (closed adds the last→first edge). rectangle: 4 walls.

points.description: Plan points in mm (segment: exactly 2; polyline: 2 or more).

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

closed.description: polyline only: also create the wall from the last point back to the first. Default false.

rectangle.description: rectangle only: corner, width, depth and rotation.

origin.description: Corner the rectangle starts from (before rotation), in mm.

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

width.description: Size along X (before rotation), in mm.

depth.description: Size along Y (before rotation), in mm.

rotation.description: Counter-clockwise rotation around the origin corner, in degrees. Default 0.

wallType.description: Wall type as "Family: Type" (e.g. "Parede básica: Alvenaria 140"), type name or id. Required: never chosen for you.

baseLevel.description: Base level by name or id.

baseOffset.description: Base offset from the base level, in mm. Default 0.

topLevel.description: Top constraint level by name or id. Give topLevel or height, not both.

topOffset.description: Top offset from topLevel, in mm (negative = below it). Only with topLevel.

height.description: Unconnected height in mm (wall not attached to a top level). Give topLevel or height, not both.

locationLine.description: Which line of the wall lies on the given points. finishFaceInterior with a closed outline makes the outline the room's inner face. Default wallCenterline.

exteriorSide.description: Closed shapes only: put each wall's exterior face outside the outline (default), inside it, or keep Revit's side from the drawing direction.

flip.description: Swap the exterior and interior faces of every wall of this item (applied after exteriorSide). Default false.

structural.description: Create structural walls. Default false (architectural partitions).

joinEnds.description: Let the walls join at their ends (corners). Default true.

continueOnError.description: false (default): any failure rolls back the whole call. true: failed items are skipped and listed in failed[].

tools.name: execute_batch
tools.description: Runs several tool calls against one document as a single atomic change: one Ctrl+Z undoes the whole batch. Every step is validated before anything runs; UI steps can't be mixed with model changes and only batchable tools are accepted (max 200 steps). Use "$steps[i].path" in args to pass a value from an earlier step (e.g. "$steps[0].changes.created[0]"). With dryRun the batch runs and is rolled back, returning what would change. The approval risk of a batch is the highest risk among its steps. Returns per-step results plus the combined change set.

steps.description: Steps to run in order, all against the same document.

tool.description: Name of a batchable framework tool, e.g. set_elements_pinned.

args.description: Arguments of that tool (without document/dryRun). A string "$steps[i].path" is replaced by a value from the result of an earlier step i, e.g. "$steps[0].changes.created[0]" or "$steps[1].data.viewId".

stopOnError.description: When true (default), the first failing step rolls the whole batch back. When false, failing steps are skipped (their own changes rolled back) and the others are kept.

tools.name: find_elements
tools.description: Find elements deterministically by category (any language: OST_Walls / Walls / Paredes), family, type, level, workset, view, bounding box in mm and parameter conditions where[] (eq, neq, contains, starts_with, ends_with, regex, gt/gte/lt/lte in wire units mm/m2/m3/deg, is_empty, not_empty), reading each parameter on the instance or its type. Returns ids, names and the requested fields, ordered by id, with an exact total and limit/offset paging (countOnly for just the count). Read-only.

categories.description: Categories, in any language: OST_Walls, Walls or Paredes. Omit for all model categories.

typeName.description: Type name, or "Family: Type" (case and accents ignored).

level.description: Level name or id: only elements associated with that level.

workset.description: Workset name or id (workshared models only).

view.description: View name or id: only elements visible in that view.

bbox.description: Only elements whose bounding box intersects this box, in mm.

x.description: X coordinate (project internal origin). Unit: mm.

y.description: Y coordinate (project internal origin). Unit: mm.

z.description: Z coordinate (project internal origin). Unit: mm.

x.description: X coordinate (project internal origin). Unit: mm.

y.description: Y coordinate (project internal origin). Unit: mm.

z.description: Z coordinate (project internal origin). Unit: mm.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

op.description: Operator (default eq). Text compares ignore case and accents; numbers compare in wire units (mm, m2, m3, deg, %).

value.description: Value to compare with (not needed for is_empty / not_empty).

scope.description: Where to read the parameter: auto (instance, then type; default), instance or type.

fields.description: Parameters to return for each element (wire units), each {guid} | {builtIn} | {name}.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

countOnly.description: Return only the exact count (default false).

tools.name: get_element_parameters
tools.description: Read the parameters of one or more elements (instance and/or type), with metadata: name, builtIn, guid, storage type, data type, group, read-only flag, value in wire units (mm, m2, m3, deg, %; ElementId values as the referenced element's name, raw id in 'raw'), and Revit's display text. Use builtIn or guid from the result to reference a parameter unambiguously in set_parameters. Elements inside links are readable with "linkInstanceId:elementId". Paged by element. Read-only.

elementIds.description: Elements to read, as strings: element id ("123456"), UniqueId, or "linkInstanceId:elementId" for an element inside a Revit link. Type ids work too.

scope.description: instance = the element's own parameters; type = its type's; both = both (default).

parameters.description: Only these parameters, each {guid} | {builtIn} | {name}. Omit for all parameters.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

includeEmpty.description: Include parameters without a value (default true).

limit.description: Maximum number of elements returned (1-200, default 50).

offset.description: Number of elements to skip, for paging (default 0).

tools.name: get_session_context
tools.description: Call first. Returns this Revit session's state: add-in version and capabilityHash (compare with the server's manifest to detect an outdated add-in), Revit version/build/language, every open document (docId, title, isFamilyDocument, isWorkshared, isActive, isReadOnly, isModified), the active document, the targeted document, the active view and the number of queued tool calls.

tools.name: set_elements_pinned
tools.description: Pins or unpins elements by id in the target document. Elements already in the requested state are reported as unchanged; ids that don't exist are reported as notFound. Undo with Ctrl+Z or by calling it again with the opposite value. Supports dryRun.

elementIds.description: Ids of the elements to pin or unpin.

pinned.description: true pins the elements (they can't be moved or deleted by accident); false unpins them.

tools.name: set_parameters
tools.description: Write instance parameter values on 1..500 elements in one transaction (one Ctrl+Z). Reference parameters by guid, builtIn or name; numbers in wire units (mm, m2, m3, deg, %), ElementId parameters by id or name. Every write is read back: values Revit changed (formulas, rounding) come back as 'mismatch'. Atomic by default. Critical parameters (type, level, phase, workset, host) are blocked unless allowCritical. Type parameters are refused here: use set_type_parameters. Undo: Ctrl+Z, or send the returned revert[] back to this tool.

items.description: Writes to apply: one {elementId, parameter, value, unit?} per value. Up to 500 per call.

elementId.description: Element id or UniqueId, as a string.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

value.description: New value. Numbers in wire units (length mm, area m2, volume m3, angle deg, slope %); yes/no as true/false; ElementId parameters take an id or a name (level, phase, material, type); null clears text and ElementId values.

unit.description: Optional unit for this number instead of the wire default: m, cm, mm, ft, in, m2, ft2, m3, l, deg, rad, %, ratio, or internal (raw Revit value).

elementIds.description: Shortcut for the same value on several elements: element ids (strings), used with parameter + value instead of items.

parameter.description: Shortcut: the parameter to write on every element of elementIds.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

value.description: Shortcut: the value to write on every element of elementIds (same rules as items[].value).

unit.description: Shortcut: optional unit override for value.

atomic.description: true (default): all or nothing — any invalid item, refused value or read-back mismatch rolls the whole call back. false: valid items are written and the rest reported in items[] with their status.

allowCritical.description: Allow parameters that change what an element is or where it lives (type, levels and constraints, phases, workset, host) and one Mark on many elements. Default false.

tools.name: set_type_parameters
tools.description: Write TYPE parameter values (affects every instance of the type; result reports instancesAffected). elementId may be a type id or an instance id (its type is used). Same rules as set_parameters: guid/builtIn/name references, wire units (mm, m2, m3, deg, %), read-back with 'mismatch', atomic by default, critical parameters blocked unless allowCritical. Needs human approval. Undo: Ctrl+Z, or send revert[] back to this tool.
